title: Import the module
prompt: Import json and define round_trip(row) using json.dumps then json.loads. Example: {"card":"Xbow"} is returned unchanged.
tests: assert round_trip({"card":"Xbow","cost":6}) == {"card":"Xbow","cost":6}, "JSON round trip must preserve this dictionary"
hint: Module imports use the name before a dot, such as json.loads.

title: Import a single function
prompt: Use from math import ceil. Define ticks_needed(seconds, tick_seconds) to round seconds / tick_seconds upward. Example: ticks_needed(1.1, 0.5) == 3. Inputs are nonnegative seconds and positive tick lengths.
tests:
assert ticks_needed(1.1,0.5) == 3, "1.1 seconds needs three half-second ticks"
assert ticks_needed(0,0.5) == 0, "zero duration needs zero ticks"
assert ticks_needed(1,0.5) == 2, "an exact duration needs no extra tick"
hint: ceil rounds upward, unlike int which discards a fractional part.

title: Use an import alias
prompt: Import json as data_json. Define decode_many(lines), ignoring whitespace-only lines. Example: ['{"derived":"LOSS"}'] returns a one-element list.
starter:
import json as data_json
def decode_many(lines):
    # TODO use the alias
    return []
tests:
assert decode_many(['{"derived":"LOSS"}'," "]) == [{"derived":"LOSS"}], "use the imported decoder and skip blanks"
assert data_json.__name__ == "json", "data_json should name the json module"
hint: The alias changes the local name, not the module itself.

title: Read a package description
prompt: Open pipeline/__init__.py as UTF-8 text, without importing pipeline. Define package_mentions(name) to return whether name occurs in that text. Example: package_mentions("Deck-agnostic") is True.
tests:
with open("pipeline/__init__.py", encoding="utf-8") as source:
    content = source.read()
for term in ["Deck-agnostic", "pipeline", "not_a_real_package_marker_991"]:
    assert package_mentions(term) == (term in content), "search the actual package description for each requested term"
hint: source.read() returns the whole text; this file is small.
